attacks.name: Compromised Producer Private Key
attacks.setup: Attacker possesses producerKey.privateKey and fabricates an internally consistent synthetic execution trajectory with fake tool output.
attacks.attackerCapability: Possession of valid producer Ed25519 signing key; knowledge of canonical schema and hash chaining rules; cannot compromise verifier keyring.
attacks.expectedSecurityProperty: Authenticity vs Independent Verification: Single authority accepts synthetic evidence; multi-authority requiring independent supervisor endorsement rejects.
attacks.conclusion: Single-authority Phase 35 cannot distinguish genuine physical execution from a compromised producer's internally consistent synthetic bundle. Multi-authority quorum requiring supervisor co-signing materially closes this vulnerability.

attacks.name: Malicious but Validly Signed Bundle
attacks.setup: Bundle contains failed attempt (exitCode: 1, status: FAILED) but falsely claims run status: COMPLETED in terminalState.
attacks.attackerCapability: Valid producer key; ability to sign arbitrary JSON payloads.
attacks.expectedSecurityProperty: Replay validity vs Cryptographic Authenticity: Replay verifier must catch false completion claim despite valid signature.
attacks.conclusion: Signatures prove producer identity, not execution truthfulness. The deterministic replay verifier independently catches the false completion claim and quarantines the bundle.

attacks.name: Valid Signature + False Operational Outcome
attacks.setup: Bundle contains non-zero exit code (exitCode: 1) on required verification action while claiming run completion.
attacks.attackerCapability: Valid producer key; internally consistent hash roots.
attacks.expectedSecurityProperty: Fourfold completion rule must independently derive terminal outcome FAILED and quarantine false COMPLETED claims.
attacks.conclusion: Phase 35 fourfold completion rule derives operational outcome independently of producer claims. Valid signature provides no bypass for unverified or failed operations.

attacks.name: Replay-Valid but Policy-Invalid Evidence
attacks.setup: Bundle is replay-valid and signed by trusted producer, but contains unredacted secret credentials in tool input payload.
attacks.attackerCapability: Valid producer key; structurally valid and replay-valid execution trajectory.
attacks.expectedSecurityProperty: Policy Conjunction: Valid signature and passing replay do not bypass secret scanning policy.
attacks.conclusion: Ingestion enforces conjunction: Status = Accepted iff ValidSignature AND ValidReplay AND ValidPolicy. Quorum adds no additional protection here.

attacks.name: Revoked Producer Authority
attacks.setup: Bundle signed while key is trusted; key subsequently revoked in TrustedKeyring; new bundle submitted with revoked key; historical bundle re-verified.
attacks.expectedSecurityProperty: Fail-closed rejection for new submissions; historical auditability preserved.
attacks.conclusion: Phase 35 cleanly separates current submission authority from historical audit integrity without retroactive destruction of past evidence.

attacks.name: Supervisor Disagreement
attacks.setup: Producer signs bundle as VERIFIED; independent supervisor disagrees and refuses to sign (or provides invalid signature).
attacks.attackerCapability: Unilateral producer signature without supervisor endorsement.
attacks.expectedSecurityProperty: 2-of-2 quorum halts ingestion (deadlock); 2-of-3 threshold allows progress if third independent witness signs.

observedResult.quorum2of3: ACCEPTED (2 distinct valid signatures: producer + witness)

attacks.conclusion: Strict 2-of-2 consensus trades availability for safety when authorities disagree. A 2-of-3 threshold provides fault tolerance against a single recalcitrant authority.

attacks.name: Conflicting Valid Evidence for Same RunId
attacks.setup: Two distinct valid bundles (exported at T1 and T2) ingested for the same runId under different content-addressed bundleIds.
attacks.attackerCapability: Valid producer key generating divergent exports or trajectories for the same logical runId.
attacks.expectedSecurityProperty: Single authority content-addressing accepts both; quorum enforces canonical consensus on bundleId.
attacks.conclusion: Phase 35 content-addressing indexes strictly by bundle content hash, allowing divergent valid bundles for the same runId to coexist in archive. Quorum signing over canonical bundleId enforces terminal consensus.

attacks.name: Signature Stripping
attacks.setup: Signature field removed from a valid signed bundle; submitted under allowUnsignedLegacy=false and allowUnsignedLegacy=true.
attacks.attackerCapability: Attacker strips signature to evade identity attribution or exploit legacy fallback.
attacks.expectedSecurityProperty: Strict mode rejects with UNSIGNED_BUNDLE_REJECTED; legacy mode accepts with UNSIGNED_LEGACY.
attacks.conclusion: Phase 35 prevents signature stripping from masquerading as verified authority.

attacks.name: Signature Substitution
attacks.setup: Signature swapped with unknown key, invalid bytes, or wrong keyId.
attacks.attackerCapability: Attacker attempts to forge authority by substituting signatures.
attacks.conclusion: Ed25519 signature verification strictly binds payload digest, public key fingerprint, and signature bytes.

attacks.name: Keyring Compromise
attacks.setup: Attacker compromises local TrustedKeyring registry and registers arbitrary rogue keys as TRUSTED.
attacks.attackerCapability: Full control over verifier's TrustedKeyring trust root.
attacks.expectedSecurityProperty: Trust Boundary Limit: Neither single authority nor multi-authority quorum can protect against trust-root compromise.

observedResult.multiAuthorityQuorumResult: ACCEPTED (both rogue keys verified as TRUSTED)

attacks.conclusion: Quorum does NOT protect against trust-root compromise. If the verifier's local keyring is subverted, the attacker can register N keys and satisfy any N-of-M quorum threshold.

attacks.name: One Malicious Authority in 2-of-3 Model
attacks.setup: Authorities A and B are honest; Authority C is malicious and issues an invalid signature.
attacks.attackerCapability: One corrupt authority in a 3-authority committee.
attacks.expectedSecurityProperty: 2-of-3 threshold establishes quorum with 2 honest signatures; corrupt signature is isolated.
attacks.conclusion: A threshold 2-of-3 quorum model maintains ingestion availability in the presence of one faulty or malicious authority.

attacks.name: Two Conflicting Honest Authorities
attacks.setup: Authority A evaluates and signs; Authority B experiences a timeout or independent verification failure and refuses to sign.
attacks.attackerCapability: Environmental non-determinism causing honest authority disagreement.
attacks.expectedSecurityProperty: 2-of-2 model deadlocks (liveness failure); quorum threshold is not reached.
attacks.conclusion: Strict multi-authority consensus trades availability for safety in non-deterministic environments, resulting in liveness failure when honest nodes disagree.

attacks.name: Duplicate Authority Signatures
attacks.setup: Attacker submits duplicate signatures from the same authority (Authority A) to satisfy a threshold of 2.
attacks.attackerCapability: Replay of genuine signature from single authority.
attacks.expectedSecurityProperty: Quorum verifier counts distinct keyIds only; duplicate keyId rejected as 1 signature.
attacks.conclusion: Quorum verification must enforce distinct authority identities; replaying duplicate signatures from one authority cannot satisfy threshold.

attacks.name: Historical Revocation
attacks.setup: Ingest valid bundle while key is TRUSTED; revoke key in keyring; verify archived bundle.
attacks.attackerCapability: Historical audit under revoked key state.
attacks.expectedSecurityProperty: Historical bundle remains VERIFIED with authorityStatus: REVOKED.
attacks.conclusion: Phase 35 architecture guarantees historical auditability without rewriting past evidence.

attacks.name: Deterministic Attack Replay
attacks.setup: Execute identical attack evaluation across 5 independent trials with fresh gateways and archives.
attacks.attackerCapability: Evaluating repeatability and determinism of security decisions.
attacks.expectedSecurityProperty: 100% deterministic decision across all repeated trials.
attacks.conclusion: Evidence verification, signature validation, and policy checks are 100% deterministic.

demonstratedGaps.title: Unilateral Producer Synthetic Evidence Fabrication
demonstratedGaps.description: A compromised producer private key allows an adversary to synthesize execution trajectories with fake observations that pass single-authority Ed25519 verification and clean-room replay verification.

demonstratedGaps.title: Multi-Bundle RunId Conflict Blindness
demonstratedGaps.description: Content-addressed ingestion accepts multiple valid bundles for the same logical runId without enforcing terminal outcome uniqueness or canonical sequencing.

demonstratedBenefits.title: Defense-in-Depth Against Producer Key Compromise
demonstratedBenefits.description: Requiring an independent supervisor endorsement (2-of-2) ensures that compromise of a worker process or worker key alone cannot introduce synthetic accepted evidence.

demonstratedBenefits.title: Fault-Tolerant Availability Under 2-of-3
demonstratedBenefits.description: A 2-of-3 threshold allows admission even if one authority goes offline, while preventing unilateral falsification.

unresolvedQuestions.title: Cross-Host Supervisor Observation Protocol
unresolvedQuestions.description: How the supervisor independently observes and validates worker execution before signing without duplicating full execution cost.

unresolvedQuestions.title: Canonical RunId Unique Constraint
unresolvedQuestions.description: Whether the archive should enforce a unique constraint on (runId, canonicalBundleId) at the persistence layer.
